Subject: Follow-up & recap — Deployment mode preferences (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Jordan / Priyanka,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the context on Acme's catalog search and personalization pilots. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the right deployment path: 

Summary of needs from the call:
- PII-sensitive data in prompts/metadata (redaction required and data residency controls).
- Peak traffic estimate: ~50 req/s during promotional peaks, baseline closer to 5–10 req/s.
- Typical request size: ~800–1,200 tokens.
- Latency requirement: sub-300ms p50 for prompt-only scoring flows, p95 target <700ms.
- Desire for isolation controls due to noisy-neighbor risk; also want clear SLOs for uptime/throughput.

Quick qualification notes on deployment options:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started, shared infra with burst capacity. Good for proof-of-concept and non-PII or where token-level retention policy suffices.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): dedicated GPU pools for your tenant with configurable throughput guarantees, predictable latency, and optional burst policies. Good middle ground when you need isolation but want Redwood-managed infra.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed networking and KMS. Best for regulated PII workloads or strict audit/compliance requirements.

Attachments: I attached a short deployment-options PDF and an initial SLA draft for your review. Also attaching the SOC2 summary per your ask.

Questions / immediate asks to help us recommend the right path:
1) Is Acme comfortable with Redwood Hosted if we enable strict retention and KMS controls, or is a fully isolated model required from day one?
2) Can you confirm whether the 50 req/s estimate is sustained or burst (and any seasonal multipliers)?
3) Any hard constraints on cross-region hosting or data residency?

Proposed next steps:
- If you want isolation but still managed infra, we recommend a 2-week Dedicated pilot with a defined throughput reservation so you can validate latency and noisy-neighbor behavior.
- If you require full tenant isolation, we can scope a Private VPC evaluation.

Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rishi (our infra lead) and Laura (CS) to go deeper on SLOs and pilot planning. What times work for you this week?

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Jordan / Priyanka — quick technical note ahead of the call tomorrow. 

Short answers up front:
- Dedicated offers tenant-dedicated GPU pools (no shared worker processes) with configurable throughput reservations. For Dedicated customers we provide a contractual throughput reservation that maps to a guaranteed number of inference slots; during pressure we prioritize tenant slots over best-effort workloads.
- Noisy-neighbor mitigations include: GPU tenant pinning, scheduler reservations, per-tenant request queues and QoS classification, cgroup-level CPU / NIC bandwidth limits, and automatic request shedding/fallback when queues exceed configured thresholds. These controls reduce noisy-neighbor risk significantly versus shared Hosted.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) provides the highest level of isolation: private control plane, VPC peering or on-prem appliance, customer KMS for keys, and no co-tenant runtime on the same hardware. This is the recommended route if you have strict audit/PII isolation requirements.

SLA & throughput notes:
- Our Dedicated offering has a baseline SLA of 99.9% availability for the inference service and standard remediation credits for outages.
- Throughput guarantees are enforced via reservation units; for your profile (baseline 10 req/s, 50 req/s burst) we typically recommend reserving capacity that covers baseline + 1.5x peak and enabling a short burst buffer for brief spikes. Exact reservation mapping depends on model size and batching behavior — I'll need model selection and avg tokens/request to provide a sizing number (I can run a quick simulation if you share that).

Operational suggestions:
- Enable KV/prefix caching for personalization to reduce repeat compute and lower peak reservation needs.
- Use batching and a short latency-aware batch window to improve GPU utilization without breaching p95 targets.
- For audit-friendly telemetry, we can configure a scrubbed audit log stream plus a separate encrypted debug log stream (the latter accessible only with explicit KMS access).

Pilot proposal:
- 2-week Dedicated pilot with a scoped reservation and observability dashboard. During pilot we'll run load profiles that emulate baseline and marketing bursts and validate p50/p95 latency and SLO behavior.
- Deliverables: sizing report, pilot runbook, observed latency/throughput charts, and recommended reservation for production.

If that sounds reasonable, we'll confirm model(s) you'll run in pilot and set up a short ingestion test so we can size accurately. See the shared runbook here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-runbook

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
